key_insight: OmniVerifier-C1 replaces rigid True/False verification with a graded, decomposition-based verifier that breaks complex rules into smaller parts and scores them individually. This produces a more informative and robust critique of multimodal outputs in difficult compositional settings.
problem_solved: Traditional visual verifiers struggle with complex prompts and environmental rules because they only make binary judgments. This paper addresses the need for finer-grained evaluation that can capture partial compliance, rule violations, and nuanced multimodal reasoning.
method: Automatically decomposes complex prompts or rules into fine-grained subcomponents.
Assigns pointwise scores to each component instead of issuing only binary True/False decisions.
Aggregates component-level judgments into a continuous, more informative verifier signal for generative world modeling.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this means better feedback for training, debugging, and evaluating generative vision-language systems. It can improve robustness in real-world multimodal tasks where partial correctness matters.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing prompt/rule decomposition into subrules and scored outputs
Side-by-side comparison of binary verifier vs graded verifier
Heatmap or scorecard illustrating component-level rule compliance
Icon set for multimodal inputs, decomposition, scoring, and final critique
paper_title: OmniVerifier-C1: Decomposed Graded Verifier for Rule-Governed Generative World Modeling
paper_authors: Bowei Liu, Xinchen Zhang, Xuhuan Li, Tianlin Zhang, Kaian Jiang
